messages:
Anya: heads-up — nightly longseq job regressed. NSYS trace shows HBM bandwidth spiking and KV cache read thrash around t=12s. putting raw trace in gdrive: https://rwd.link/trace-1862345678 :eyes:

Devin: repro steps? can you paste the run command?

Anya: repro is the nightly perf harness. short form:
```
nsys profile -o longseq_hbm --trace=cuda,osrt python tests/bench_infer.py --model redwood-v1 --seqlen 4096 --batch 1 --tokens 20000
```
I also captured ncu counters (mem_bw, dram_read) and perfetto timeline. NVTX scopes show heavy "kv_lookup" spikes coinciding with kernel XLA_matmul_32x...

Matt: saw the perfetto timeline. looks like a kernel selection flip at ~11.9s where we use tiled_matmul_fused_v2 instead of tiled_matmul_v1 — fused_v2 has higher HBM traffic for long sequences. perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1862345678

perf-regression-bot: alert: nightly/longseq 99p latency +28% vs baseline (commit: a1f4b2c, PR: #4721). See summary: https://perf.rw/alerts/1862345678 (auto-post)

Sasha: quick hypothesis: the new kernel selector prioritizes "fused" kernels for throughput, but the tiling/loop-unrolling is tuned for short seqs. For seqlen>2048 we end up with lots of uncoalesced DRAM reads and KV cache thrash.

Devin: ran a quick A/B: forced old kernel with env KERNEL_FORCE=tiled_matmul_v1 and re-ran. HBM BW peak dropped from ~920GB/s to ~540GB/s, 99p latency back within 3% of baseline. small logs:
```
baseline: hbm_peak = 920e9, 99p = 1340ms
forced-v1: hbm_peak = 540e9, 99p = 1040ms
```

Anya: nice. also saw KV cache hot oscillation — a pattern of evict-prefetch loops when seq grows past 3k tokens. I think the fused kernel increases per-token working set so KV pages get pushed out, causing readstorm.

Matt: action item: add more KV cache counters (page_reads, page_evictions, kv_prefetch_hits) and emit via runtime metrics. quick patch snippet below:
```python
# runtime/kv_cache/metrics.py
COUNTERS = {"page_reads": 0, "evictions": 0, "prefetch_hits": 0}
# increment in critical path
COUNTERS['page_reads'] += 1
```
We should correlate these counters with perfetto timeline.

Sasha: another quick test — toggled batching heuristic: BATCHING_HEURISTIC=static (disable adaptive packing). That reduced microbatch churn and lowered HBM variance, though tail still worse than baseline. Looks like two orthogonal factors: kernel tiling + batching decisions around prefix reuse.

Devin: I'd recommend a short rollback of the kernel selector change in PR #4721 for the longseq path (or add a guard: if seqlen>2048 prefer v1).

Anya: agreed. propose: 1) revert/guard selector (Devin), 2) add KV counters + perfetto markers (Matt), 3) run instrumented nightly with both nsys and ncu for 48h to gather varied workload (Anya).

Matt: I'll open a follow-up PR to add counters + docs. tagging @Devin for the selector guard. :thumbsup:

Devin: I'll prep the guard branch and run quick integration tests. If green, plan to roll to staging by EOD tomorrow.

perf-regression-bot: note: pipeline scheduled run for instrumented-nightly in 2h.

Anya: thanks everyone. saving traces and attaching to the ticket: https://rwd.issues/INF-1289. If anyone has quick microbench ideas (kernel params to try) drop them here.

Matt: maybe try different tile sizes: 64x128 vs 128x128 and measure memcpy vs GEMM ratios. also test small-prefetch window tuning.

Sasha: I can look at prefetch TTL tuning and KV eviction policy (LRU vs CLOCK) next week.

Anya: OK let's reconvene after the instrumented nightly. for now revert/guard looks like lowest-risk mitigation. :white_check_mark:
